title: Idempotency: how to prevent duplicate payments/orders

slides.headline:
Idempotency:
Make retries
*safe.*

One customer.
==Three== charges.
slides.sub:
The client never sent three requests.
**It sent one, then retried twice.**

slides.label: What actually happened
slides.headline:
The response died,
not the write
slides.desc: Your server committed the charge. The connection dropped before the response came back. The client saw a timeout and did the only sensible thing it could. It retried.

slides.headline: The retry storm
slides.hand: A timeout is not a failure.
slides.callout: A timeout tells you the response is missing. It never tells you the write didn't happen.

slides.label: The fix
slides.headline: Give every attempt a name
slides.desc: One key per **intent**, not per attempt. The same key rides every retry.

bad.verdict: Every retry looks like a brand new order.

good.verdict: Every retry resolves to the same order.

slides.label: The bug in every tutorial
slides.headline:
The loser has
nothing to replay
slides.desc: The winner hasn't finished yet, so no response is stored. Returning **200** here tells the client the payment succeeded before it actually has.

items: Replay **only** when the stored status is `done`
**409 Conflict** while the winner is still in flight
This is what **Stripe** returns in the same case

slides.headline: Claim the key *first*
slides.note: The unique index arbitrates, not your code. Claim it in its own transaction, never the one doing the charge.

slides.headline: Two retries, *one row*
slides.code:
CREATE TABLE idempotency_keys (
  key        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  status     TEXT NOT NULL,
  response   JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Two retries in the same millisecond both hit
-- this index. Exactly one INSERT survives.
slides.note: No lock. No queue. No distributed coordinator. One `PRIMARY KEY` does the arbitration for you.

slides.headline:
A retry is not
a new request.
It is the *same intent*,
asking again.
slides.sub: Design every write endpoint so the second attempt is boring.
